title: Ordered delta reconciliation and idempotent replay for multiplexed event streams
creator: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: hosts using our streaming API observe out-of-order fragments and duplicated tool-call frames after network flaps and proxy-induced replays. This ticket defines a reconciliation model for multiplexed streams (multiple logical channels per connection), a compact chunk header format that enables idempotent replays, and server/client negotiation for reconnection recovery without corrupting ongoing function/tool calls or structured outputs. Goals: (1) deterministic ordering at consumer level for deltas across channels, (2) ability to safely replay a small tail of chunks without double-applying effects, (3) minimal on-wire overhead and backwards compatibility with existing clients. Non-goals: redesigning transport (we continue to use HTTP/SSE or eventstream), replacing higher-level application semantics for idempotency outside the stream protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Chunk header with (channel_id, monotonically increasing seq, fragment_id, checksum, partial_flag) defined and implemented in runtime-1.20
Server and client perform reconnection handshake using last-ack metadata; server can provide a compact replay window (<= 32 chunks)

Tool/function calls that were in-flight at disconnect are either resumed safely (if last committed frame found) or aborted with an explicit terminal frame. No duplicate function-execution observable by API consumer in 99.99% of flaps.
End-to-end integration tests covering multiplexed channels with interleaved structured outputs and function-call frames pass in CI
Metrics and dashboard show <0.01% increase in user-observed duplicate outputs after rollout to Canary tenants
implementation_notes: Chunk header fields: channel_id (8-bit logical channel), seq (64-bit monotonic per-channel), frag_idx (16-bit index for multi-part chunk), checksum (CRC32), tail_flag (boolean encoded as 1 bit)
On write: runtime attaches header and persists a 32-entry recent-chunk index per connection to support quick replays without full storage hits

On reconnect: client sends last_seen map {channel_id: last_seq}. Server computes overlapping window and returns 'replay-start' token plus an ordinal base. Server will not replay past the retention window; if gap > window then server returns 'gap-abort' with guidance to reinitialize conversation

Function/tool-call semantics: a function-call begins with a tool-call-open chunk that includes a call_id. Tool-call is considered durable/committed once a terminal tool-call-success or tool-call-failure chunk is emitted and acked. If client reconnects and last_seen < commit_seq for that call_id, the server will either (a) replay the missing fragments idempotently (server must ensure the function execution is not re-triggered) or (b) emit a tool-call-abort chunk if the execution cannot be reconciled. The runtime will prefer (a) whenever an execution result was persisted during the short replay window.

Backward compatibility: servers will accept clients that do not send last_seen (legacy clients). For legacy clients server will fall back to existing behavior (best-effort streaming without guaranteed de-duplication). New clients detect server capability via handshake header X-RW-Stream-Capabilities: delta-recon=v2
Negotiation: keep handshake inexpensive (single HTTP GET with optional header); runtime will add a small config flag 'enable_delta_recon' default off for dedicated/private until validated by canary
test_plan: Unit tests for chunk encode/decode and checksum validation
Integration harness: simulate 500 concurrent multiplexed streams with randomized disconnects and proxy replay; assert ordering and de-duplication invariants
Chaos test: inject out-of-order packet delivery and verify client state machine idempotency
End-to-end: verify function-call at-most-once observable semantics for repeated reconnect sequences
Compatibility test matrix: legacy client -> v2 server, v2 client -> legacy server, v2 client -> v2 server
rollout_plan: Feature branch + runtime unit tests merged to main
Deploy runtime-1.20 to staging; enable feature flag; run integration harness overnight
Canary rollout to 3 high-traffic tenants for 72 hours; monitor duplicate-output and P50/P95 streaming latency
Gradual enablement for Dedicated and Private customers after opt-in; defaulting off for Private until compliance review complete
Full rollout and SDK updates for JS/Python with migration doc
comments: 2025-02-18 Asha Patel: Initial triage - customer SRE reported repeated chat replays after Istio sidecar reconnects. Prior attempts to dedupe at client found brittle. Proposing a wire-level reconciliation header to give servers deterministic view.

2025-02-21 Maya Chen (runtime): early prototype shows ~15% increase in per-connection memory due to recent-chunk index; acceptable for hosted but needs a bounded configuration for Dedicated. Added config 'recon_window_size' (default 32).

2025-02-26 Design review notes: PM requests explicit guidance for SDKs on how to surface gap-abort vs full reset. UX owner suggests adding 'streaming_state' event for clients to display 'reconnecting - replaying' vs 'reconnecting - missing history'.

2025-03-01 Jonah Ruiz: POC run on staging with 2000 concurrent streams and synthetic flaps. Observed 0.002% duplicate tool-call executions when recon_window_size=32 and persistence enabled; duplicates traced to non-atomic persist path in task worker. Filed followup ENG-275422 for durable commit behavior.
